Anyone with questions on what I went through or want to talk about themselves, family, or friends that went through treatment.
I AMA childhood and adult cancer survivor. Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia and a Type 3 Astrocytoma Brain Tumor.
How many months would you say you've been sick for? What did people do to make that time better for you?

Chemo was three years when I was a kid. Diagnosed at 6 in 1991. The Astrocytoma was about a year of treatment. Chemo plus radiation for the first six months if I remember the time right. Then just chemo for 1 week a month after that.

The nice part about the chemo for the brain tumour was that it was just a pill and radiation is painless.

Even though the drugs were shit as a kid I did the make-a-wish thing. Met various local celebrities and athletes. Plus camp Goodtimes, summer camp for children who have or had cancer.

As an adult my wife,family and friends kept me busy and I found various hobbies while away from work. I was never interested in support groups while sick but always make myself available to anyone now that I am in remission.
Would you say fighting cancer is a part of your identity, or do you like to focus on other parts of your life?

Oddly it is. There were a lot of things I got to do because of it and there is a tight knit group of us long term survivors that were in the hospital and/or at camp together.

I think it has given me the ability to stay very calm and collected in difficult situations. I think that throws some people off.
What is your opinion of Lance Armstrong, and does it differ from other long term cancer survivors?
does that mean you HAVE a brain tumor, or you HAD a brain tumor?
There is a little piece of dead tissue still there and they monitor change. It's name is Tyrel and we have a party for it every year.
have you participated in the social support community? if so, are you glad you did?

In the second go around I really just wanted to get going with my life. I found being around family and friends was the best for me. That was my personal feeling but I know others need different support services. Everyone copes diffidently. However now that I have done this a few times I will always talk about my experiences to anyone that asks. If my story helps raise money for research or support services I am always willing to tell it.
What was your treatment method? Did you have any symptoms or side effects? What were they? Do you have annual checkups or blood work now?
I get an MRI yearly now along with bloodwork.
a lot is made of which organizations (American Cancer Society, Susan G. Komen, etc.) do a better job of shepherding funds toward research. as a survivor, do you have strong feelings about this?

I am strongly in support of research and support services. Awareness is great but sometimes it gets overdone like the pink ribbons. I'm Canadian so we have the Canadian Cancer Society and I was involved with Leukemia and Lymphoma society back when they were the Leukemia Research Fund.

I have also been involved in fundraising event promotion with the Canadian Cancer Society. They run Camp Goodtimes in my province.

Did your brain tumor cause you to experience hallucinations?

If yes, could you describe them?

Nope. Was just about to go for a drive with my wife and started to get a drunk feeling and sat down on the couch. Had a seizure and can remember getting loaded into an ambulance. Then waking at the local hospital. Going to the washroom and then waking up at a different hospital.

Interesting.

Did you get to keep the tumors once they removed them?
An Astrocytoma is more like a thin membrane. I had a brain biopsy but the radiation and chemo did all the work. Yay science and research. I did ask the doc about getting a piece but no go.
Were you diagnosed with T-cell or B-cell for ALL?
I don't recall which. I was lucky that I was able to avoid getting a bone marrow transplant.
